While Apple's annual September iPhone event is still roughly two months away, this year will be different. In September, Apple won't unveil its entire iPhone lineup all at once — instead, it will debut only the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and an all-new foldable iPhone.

The iPhone Lineup Keeps Expanding

The iPhone lineup has been steadily growing over the past few years. Not long ago, just three new models launched each year: the iPhone 11, iPhone 11 Pro, and iPhone 11 Pro Max. By 2020, with the addition of the iPhone 12 mini, the annual count rose to four. In 2022, the iPhone 12 mini was replaced by the iPhone 14 Plus, later succeeded by the iPhone Air.

With the introduction of the iPhone 16e, the yearly lineup has now grown to five models. Once the iPhone Ultra arrives, Apple's annual iPhone lineup will expand to six models. With that many devices, the stage would certainly feel crowded launching them all at once.

So Apple has decided on a staggered rollout.

Two iPhone Launches: Fall and Spring

The iPhone 18 lineup will consist of six models: iPhone 18, iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone 18e, iPhone Air 2, and iPhone Ultra.

The logic behind this staggered approach is clear: flagship models debut in the fall, while mid-range and entry-level models arrive in the spring. Here's how it breaks down:

  • Fall 2026: iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone Ultra
  • Spring 2027: iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, iPhone Air 2

Whenever the iPhone lineup has expanded to four models, that extra model has never sold well — whether it's the iPhone mini or the iPhone Plus. So Apple figures it's perfectly reasonable to clearly separate the lineup and give that extra model its own moment in the spotlight.

The situation with the iPhone 18 will be slightly different, though. Reports suggest Apple is working to unify the production process for the iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e, so the differences between the two phones may be significantly narrowed.

It's unclear at this point whether this approach will mean major upgrades for the iPhone 18e or downgrades for the iPhone 18 — but the line between the two phones may ultimately come down to details like the display panel and camera.

The Bottom Line

In summary, assuming the iPhone Air doesn't get discontinued eventually (which of course I hope it doesn't) — this is the new shape of the iPhone lineup going forward. Three in the fall, three in the spring. The end goal is to let Apple better stagger product launches and get devices into the hands of the consumers they're best suited for.

Another likely outcome is that the average selling price of iPhones will rise, since anyone wanting to ride the wave of new hardware will inevitably have to buy the iPhone 18 Pro rather than a cheaper model.

Whether this staggered approach actually drives sales across all models remains to be seen, but these are some initial thoughts.

What are your thoughts on Apple's staggered iPhone strategy? Do you buy a new iPhone in the fall or wait until spring? Drop your takes in the comments.
